summary_paragraph: A 58-year-old woman with alcoholic and HCV-related cirrhosis, metastatic hepatocellular carcinoma, and brain and likely bone metastases was admitted for severe headache, nausea, vomiting, and mild confusion. Initial imaging showed no new intracranial hemorrhage or mass effect, and MRI confirmed stability of prior brain metastases with post-treatment changes. Abdominal CT revealed new arterially enhancing liver lesions of uncertain significance, slight enlargement of a retroperitoneal lymph node, and progression of a lytic lesion in the S1 vertebra. She was found to have hypovolemia and metabolic acidosis, managed with IV fluids. A urine culture showed gram-positive bacteria, prompting a short antibiotic course despite negative blood cultures. Her symptoms improved with supportive care, and she was discharged home with plans for oncology follow-up regarding possible spine radiation and monitoring of liver lesions. Her DNR status was reaffirmed, and medication adherence, particularly with laxatives, was emphasized.
